title: onprem-deploy-healthcheck-and-fallback-procedures
content:
Purpose: compact on‑prem/VPC smoke test + troubleshooting playbook for common install/runtime failures and an upgrade precheck/rollback checklist. This is intended for oncall, SREs, and engineers performing private deploy installs or upgrades (VPC and air-gapped on‑prem flavors).

Scope: covers initial post-deploy smoke checks, quick diagnostic commands, Terraform module notes and common pitfalls, pre-upgrade validations, stepwise upgrade checklist, and fast rollback options. Not an exhaustive K8s troubleshooting guide; links to deeper runbooks are at the bottom.

Quick golden rules (read before doing anything):
- Always snapshot or export state (Terraform state + DB snapshots + VM/volume snapshots) before upgrades.
- If symptoms are service-wide, preserve logs (journalctl, container logs, kube events) before restarting components.
- Keep an approved fallback image/tag and Terraform state archive in an accessible S3/backups store.

Post-install smoke checks (first 15 minutes):
1) Control plane and services
   - systemd-based: sudo systemctl status redwood-control.service redwood-runtime.service 
   - journalctl -u redwood-control -u redwood-runtime --since "10m" | tail -n 200
   - Expected: services in "active (running)", no repeated crash loops.
2) Containers/K8s\   - If Docker/Containerd: docker ps --format '{{.Names}} {{.Image}} {{.Status}}' | grep redwood || ctr -n k8s.io containers ls\   - If Kubernetes: kubectl get pods -n redwood -o wide\   - kubectl describe pod <bad-pod> and kubectl logs <pod> -c inference-runtime\3) Health endpoints\   - curl -fsS http://localhost:8080/health || curl -fsS https://internal-api.redwood.local/health\   - Expected JSON: {"status":"ok","components":["db","queue","runtime"]} or similar.
4) Basic API sanity\   - Small generate: curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello","max_tokens":5}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'\   - Embeddings quick check: curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/embeddings -d '{"input":"test"}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'\   - Expect HTTP 200 and quick non-empty payloads.
5) GPU/Driver sanity (if using GPUs)\   - nvidia-smi should list devices and no driver errors: sudo nvidia-smi -q | head\   - docker run --gpus all --rm nvidia/cuda:11.7-base nvidia-smi\   - If nvidia-smi missing or containers fail to start with "no GPU devices" -> check nvidia-container-runtime and driver compatibility.
6) Networking basics\   - ip a (interface up), ip route, iptables -L or nft list rules\   - Check MTU: ip link show <iface> (MTU mismatches can cause gRPC fragmented frames + timeouts)\   - From a client host: curl "https://api.example.company:443/health" -v to validate TLS handshake and SNI.

Common failure signatures and quick remediation notes:
- CrashLoopBackOff / OOMKilled on runtime pods\  Symptom: pod restarts repeatedly, OOM message in events.\  Quick check: kubectl describe pod <pod> | grep -A4 Events; kubectl top pod <pod>\  Remediation: increase memory in node pool / cgroup limits, or apply temporary pod resource override and restart. Check for runaway eval loop in user-provided prompt.
\- TLS handshake failures to control plane\  Symptom: clients report "tls: handshake failure" or "certificate has expired"\  Quick check: openssl s_client -connect host:443 -servername api.example.company -showcerts\  Remediation: validate CA bundle mounted, rotate certs from PKI, ensure system clock is correct (NTP).
\- gRPC UNAVAILABLE / stream resets across many requests\  Symptom: intermittent errors, timeouts, high retries\  Quick check: look for MTU/fragmentation (tcpdump -vv -i <iface> port 443), long TCP retransmits, or overloaded proxy (envoy/nginx) logs.\  Remediation: adjust MTU, increase proxy worker threads, or route traffic to fallback model variant.
\- Model server reports "KV cache corrupted" or high cold start latency\  Symptom: huge latency on first requests, or runaway memory growth\  Quick check: runtime logs grep "KV cache"; check disk usage for cache dirs; verify quantization profile loaded matches model artifact.\  Remediation: clear prefix cache directories (move to tmp), restart runtime with --clear-kv; re-deploy model artifact built with correct quantization profile.
\- Terraform apply errors: "provider version mismatch" or state conflicts\  Symptom: terraform plan/apply fails with version/locks/permission errors\  Quick check: terraform version && terraform providers lock -check\  Remediation: pin provider versions in root module, ensure backend (S3/Dynamo or GCS/locks) is accessible, run terraform init -upgrade with care. If state lock stuck, use terraform force-unlock <LOCK_ID> only after verifying no active operations.

Terraform module notes and common pitfalls (short):\- Key module names (examples): module "redwood_private_vpc", module "redwood_onprem_cluster", module "redwood_kms_integration"\- Important variables to review before apply: var.cidr_base, var.admin_allowed_cidrs, var.kube_node_pools, var.gpu_profile, var.kms_key_arn, var.ca_cert_pem\- Backend/state: we rely on S3 (prod) + DynamoDB lock or GCS + KMS for encrypted state in air-gapped flows. Always verify backend accessibility: aws s3 ls s3://redwood-terraform-states/prod/ || gsutil ls gs://redwood-terraform-states/prod/\- Provider pinning: lock aws, google, azurerm provider versions. Mismatched providers across machines cause diffs.\- Module upgrade footgun: do NOT change module inputs that recreate stateful resources (eg: rds identifier, volume ids) without snapshot and migration plan documented.\- Drift detection: run terraform plan against the canonical workspace to detect drift; consider using terraform show -json + jq to capture diffs for review.

Pre-upgrade validation checklist (run 24h and 1h before):
- 24h before:\  - Verify backups: DB dumps exist, S3 exports listed, and restore test documented.\  - Confirm upstream images available in private registry (for air-gapped: ensure images staged locally).\  - Verify incident rotation and oncall coverage for upgrade window.\  - Run full smoke test suite results saved to artifacts store.
\- 1h before:\  - terraform plan and save plan output to artifact: terraform plan -var-file=prod.tfvars -out upgrade.plan\  - Verify cluster autoscaler disabled or set min==current to avoid pod churn.\  - Snapshot VM volumes / take etcd snapshots if using K8s control plane.\  - Verify KMS key access for model deployment secrets.\  - Warm caches: run a small batch of representative requests against runtime to populate caches.

Stepwise upgrade actions (example high-level):
1) Put system in maintenance mode (disable external load balancers, set low TTL on DNS if applicable).\2) Apply infra changes with terraform using saved plan: terraform apply "upgrade.plan"\3) Monitor resource creation: watch terraform apply output and simultaneously tail (journalctl and kube events)\4) Update runtime images via orchestrated rolling update (K8s: kubectl rollout status deployment/redwood-runtime -n redwood)\5) Run post-deploy smoke tests (see below)\6) If any critical test fails, initiate rollback (see rollback section)

Post-upgrade smoke test (10–20 min):
- Health endpoint and small generate tests (as in Post-install smoke checks)\- End-to-end model path: call generate->embed->rerank chain and assert non-empty outputs\- Performance sanity: run 5 concurrent small generates and ensure 95th percentile latency is within expected SLO (example: < 1s for local prompt length 32).\- Cost telemetry: check token counters and ensure no runaway tokenization or logging spikes.

Rollback strategies (fast):
- Terraform rollback: if you saved prior plan and previous state, you can restore previous state file (careful) and apply previous plan. Typical safe option: use last known-good Terraform configuration branch and apply to revert only the changed resources.\- Image rollback: force rollout to previous image tag in orchestrator (kubectl set image deployment/redwood-runtime redwood-runtime=registry/redwood/runtime:v1.8.3)\- Volume/DB restore: restore DB from snapshot if migration caused schema issues.

Escalation matrix (who to call):
- Tier 1: oncall SRE (primary slack: @oncall-sre)\- Tier 2: eng-private-deployments leads: Miguel Santos, Jing Wei\- Tier 3: runtime/serving team: Priya Rao, Tom Baker

Diagnostic one-liners you can run immediately:
- Check service status: sudo systemctl list-units --state=failed\- Check recent redwood logs: journalctl -u redwood-runtime -n 500 --no-pager | sed -n '1,200p'\- Show container restarts: kubectl get pods -n redwood -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,RESTARTS:.status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount
- Terraform quick verify: terraform init && terraform validate && terraform plan -var-file=prod.tfvars -out /tmp/verify.plan\- Verify KMS encrypt/decrypt: aws kms encrypt --key-id "$KMS_KEY_ARN" --plaintext "test" --query CiphertextBlob --output text | base64 -d | aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb:///dev/stdin --query Plaintext --output text

Notes on observability during incidents:
- Increase log level on runtime if reproducing an error: set ENV LOG_LEVEL=debug (or patch deployment) for a narrow window and capture logs.\- Ensure traces from clients include request-id headers; use those to correlate logs across services.

Where this doc points for deeper troubleshooting (links):
- CONFLUENCE: RDW-PRIVATE-DEPLOY-RUNBOOK (full runbooks and longer playbooks)\- K8S: RDW-K8S-DEBUG-GUIDE (pod eviction, volume attach/detach, storageclass issues)\- TF: terraform-modules/README.md (module contract and variable definitions)

Open questions / TODOs for next revision:
- Add concrete sample terraform variable files for air-gapped installs (prod + staging).\- Add automated smoke test script (bash/python) that runs the entire checklist and uploads artifacts.\- Formalize SLO numeric thresholds and include an automated pre-upgrade gating job.

Appendix: useful regexes and log snippets to search for quickly:
- CrashLoopBackOff: grep -E "CrashLoopBackOff|OOMKilled"\- TLS cert issues: grep -E "certificate.*expired|x509: certificate|tls: handshake"\- GPU errors: grep -E "cuda|nvidia|no devices|driver"

Saved artifacts location examples:
- s3://redwood-internal-private-artifacts/<cluster>-smoke-20251104-<run-id>/results.json
- gs://redwood-internal-private-artifacts/<cluster>-smoke-20251104-<run-id>/logs.tgz

Contact/owner note: Asha Patel (eng-private-deployments) — please update after any upgrade that modifies Terraform modules or runtime startup flags.
